description:
FILED s540b (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-13), docs/speed-low-hanging-review-s540.md THE LIST.  Code sha 05806e16.

WHERE: cl/pcl-runtime.lisp `%p-maybe-autoflush` (~line 4084): `(and (plusp (hash-table-count *p-autoflush-handles*)) (gethash stream *p-autoflush-handles*))`.  The count guard keeps programs that never set `$|` free; one `$| = 1` (STDOUT -- an everyday idiom) makes the count 1 for the rest of the run, and from then on every print to every handle pays a gethash on a :weakness :key table, which in SBCL takes the global system lock (the #4061 / #4501 / #4525 family).

MEASUREMENT (scratch/s540b/rp/fprint0.pl vs afprint.pl: 1 M `print $fh "x\n"` to /dev/null, the second with `$| = 1;` on STDOUT -- $fh itself is NOT autoflushed, so the only difference is the probe; ab.pl --emit, best of 7, legs/leg2.log, load 1.3): 0.074 -> 0.134 s whole run, +81.1 % (C/A -3.1 %).  ~60 ns per print.

THE FIX (runtime only): keep the autoflush mark where a probe is free -- e.g. a short simple-vector of the (at most a few) autoflushed streams compared with EQ, the stream dropped from it at close and at `$| = 0`; or a slot/plist mark on PCL's own stream wrapper if there is one.  The weak table exists so an abandoned handle is not pinned: removal at close (and at the handle's scope exit, #2006(b)) covers that; a handle abandoned WITHOUT close stays in a vector of a few entries, which is bounded by the number of handles a program ever set `$|` on.

BAR: the autoflush guard rows (grep -l 'autoflush\|\$|' Pl/t), io companion one-file runs (io/print.t-family), the measurement above reproduced (expect afprint ~= fprint0), gate.

DO NOT: drop the count guard -- programs without `$|` must stay at zero cost; do not flush on every print.

=== s540 (2026-11-13) === scheduled: s540/s540d-prompt.md (the USER: the speed fixing is a normal task).
subject: PERF (s540b, measured): once ANY handle has `$|` set (`$| = 1;` at the top of a script), EVERY print to ANY handle probes the WEAK table *p-autoflush-handles* (SBCL's global lock) -- 1 M prints to a file +81 % (0.074 -> 0.134 s); a #4061 sibling
